claim_summary: EpiCoach uses an evidence-gated temporal hypothesis loop and a wrist-only mechanistic twin to choose safety-constrained training experiments, with predictions sealed before rides and beliefs updated only from logged fits.

claim_evidence.quote: Claims about the athlete live in an evidence-gated hypothesis registry: each must issue a probabilistic prediction about a future session before it occurs, and its belief moves only through computed evidence from a logged statistical fit.

modules.name: Evidence-gated hypothesis registry and prediction ledger
modules.scope_reason: GTS: the registry preserves hypotheses, predictions, fits and lineage, and its timestamps and data cutoffs determine whether evidence is available; changing the task would not change this temporal availability logic.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - the registry does not embed a task output objective
R3_2_GTS:yes - it depends on timestamps, data cutoffs and information availability
R4:Memory and Context; Planning and Orchestration
R8:inferred - cross-task reuse follows from its temporal state and interface

evidence.quote: 1) A prediction ledger, not a chat log. Every hypothesis in the registry must emit a probabilistic prediction about a specific future ride, timestamped before the ride. Beliefs move only through a tool that requires a logged statistical fit.

modules.name: Information-directed, safety-gated workout design
modules.scope_reason: TSK: the core objective is to prescribe the next training week by trading information gain against performance gain under workload, heart-rate, readiness and illness constraints; changing the task family changes the workout objective and feasible action space.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - it embeds the training-prescription objective and safety validation criterion
R4:Planning and Orchestration; Tools and Execution

evidence.quote: The agent prescribes the next training week as a constrained experiment maximizing information gain subject to load and safety constraints, around two instrument rides.

modules.name: Wrist-only mechanistic physiological twin
modules.scope_reason: TSK: the heart-rate response, fitness-fatigue and descent-skill models produce the segment and ride outcomes used by the paper’s forecasting contract; changing the task family changes the modeled outcomes and instruments.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - the model embeds the physiological forecasting output and its instruments

evidence.quote: 2) A mechanistic twin from a watch alone. We infer, from optical heart rate, GPS and barometric altitude only, a lagged heart-rate response with drift and heat interactions, a fitness–fatigue model whose time constants are estimated rather than assumed, and a latent technical-skill state

modules.name: Rolling-origin replay benchmark for individualized physiology
modules.scope_reason: TSK: the benchmark defines next-week physiological forecast targets and forecast-comparison scoring, so its temporal state and validation criterion must be redesigned for a different task family.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - targets and scores are bound to physiological forecasting

evidence.quote: We evaluate the system two ways over eighteen months of data. A rolling-origin replay benchmark shows the twin beats standard forecasters on heart rate but not segment time, and the agentic loop matches a static model.

process_validity.quote: the gate was moved to the athlete’s lap-press point, the correction was logged as a registry event, and the forecast was changed from a historical median to the skill-model posterior.

temporal_validity.quote: The twin is refit once per week, after all of that week’s predictions have been scored and before the next are sealed, so no prediction is ever made by a model that has seen the ride it predicts.

task_performance.quote: Across 60 origins the agentic system matches the static twin on HR forecasting (CRPS 7.00 vs 7.03, p = 0.63) and segment time (0.050 vs 0.048, p = 0.007, marginally worse).
